concept.name: Queue imbalance
concept.definition: The normalized difference between the displayed size at the best bid and the best ask, a short-horizon predictor of mid-price movements: when one side of the inside market is heavier, the price tends to move toward the lighter side. It is the state variable underlying Stoikov's (2018) micro-price and relates to the order-flow imbalance of Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov.
concept.intuition: A heavy bid queue and a thin ask queue mean sellers face little resistance - the price is more likely to tick up than down.
concept.mechanics: Computed from top-of-book sizes at each order book event; positive imbalance predicts upticks with a probability that Stoikov estimates from transition matrices of imbalance and spread states, and its information decays within milliseconds to seconds.
concept.formula: QI = (Q_bid - Q_ask) / (Q_bid + Q_ask), in [-1, 1], where Q_bid and Q_ask are displayed sizes at the best bid and ask.
concept.failure_modes: Predictive power collapses when displayed size is cancelable or spoofed, around news jumps, and when the spread is wide; the signal is also crowded and degrades after latency and fees.
concept.misconceptions: Queue imbalance is a weak, short-lived statistical signal, not a standalone profitable trading rule; its in-sample edge typically fails to survive execution costs and queue-position realities.
concept.example: With 2,000 shares bid and 500 offered at the inside, QI = (2000-500)/(2000+500) = +0.6, tilting the microprice toward the ask.

citations.source: Stoikov, 'The Micro-Price: A High-Frequency Estimator of Future Prices', Quantitative Finance 18(12):1959-1966 (Crossref record DOI 10.1080/14697688.2018.1489139)
Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov, 'The Price Impact of Order Book Events', Journal of Financial Econometrics 12(1):47-88 (arXiv preprint)
